articles.title: Why Intl.DateTimeFormat('zh-CN-u-ca-chinese') Gets 2027 Chinese New Year Wrong by 1 Day (The 23:56 CST vs 00:56 JST Boundary)
articles.excerpt: If you are building a calendar renderer, scheduling tool, or printable wall planner for 2027, relying blindly on Intl.DateTimeFormat('zh-CN-u-ca-chinese') will ship an off-by-one bug for Chinese New Y…
articles.body: If you are building a calendar renderer, scheduling tool, or printable wall planner for 2027, relying blindly on Intl.DateTimeFormat('zh-CN-u-ca-chinese') will ship an off-by-one bug for Chinese New Year across a wide swath of browsers and operating systems. I hit this exact edge case while validating 2027 lunisolar grid layouts for print output. The root cause is not a casual typo in a locale file. It sits at a razor-thin four-minute astronomical boundary. The 23:56 CST vs. 00:56 JST Boundary Under the traditional Chinese lunisolar calendar, the first day of every lunar month—the shuòrì (朔日)—is the calendar date in China Standard Time (CST, UTC+8) on which the astronomical new moon (exact Sun–Moon ecliptic conjunction) occurs.

articles.title: What Is RAG in AI? Retrieval-Augmented Generation Explained
articles.excerpt: RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation. Before a language model answers, the system searches your own documents, takes the passages that match the question, and puts them into the prompt. The m…
articles.body: RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation. Before a language model answers, the system searches your own documents, takes the passages that match the question, and puts them into the prompt. The model then writes its answer from those passages instead of from memory. It is the standard way to make an AI system answer with your product facts, your policies and your procedures, and to keep those answers current when the documents change. Why RAG exists A large language model only knows the text it was trained on. Your return policy, this year's product versions and last week's troubleshooting fix were never in that text. Retraining a model every time a document changes is slow and expensive. RAG solves it at answer time: the model stays the same, and the facts arrive with each question.

articles.title: How much VRAM do you need to fine-tune an LLM?
articles.excerpt: Full fine-tuning with AdamW needs about 16 bytes of GPU memory per parameter, LoRA just over 2 and QLoRA under 1, plus a few GB of activations per sequence. Nodus fine-tuning jobs pick their GPU from…
articles.body: Full fine-tuning with AdamW needs about 16 bytes of GPU memory per parameter, LoRA just over 2 and QLoRA under 1, plus a few GB of activations per sequence. Nodus fine-tuning jobs pick their GPU from presets matched to the model and method, but the numbers are worth knowing: an 8B model needs about 135 GB for full fine-tuning, 21 GB for LoRA and 11 GB for QLoRA. A 70B model needs about 1,136 GB, 152 GB and 50 GB, assuming one 4,096-token sequence per GPU with gradient checkpointing on. This is the sizing method for any model size. Our 70B VRAM breakdown goes deeper on that one size, and LoRA vs QLoRA covers the quality and speed side of the choice.

articles.title: Balancing AI code generation speed with personal comprehension and mental ownership
articles.excerpt: The Quiet Unease of Unread Code High-throughput AI coding agents alter the rate at which source artifacts enter a repository, creating a structural mismatch between code synthesis rate and human compr…
articles.body: The Quiet Unease of Unread Code High-throughput AI coding agents alter the rate at which source artifacts enter a repository, creating a structural mismatch between code synthesis rate and human comprehension rate. When an engineer refuses to ship uninspected code, that friction should not be misdiagnosed as a neurotic bottleneck or an arbitrary personal quirk; it reflects a clash between sustainable engineering discipline and the illusion of brute-force velocity, driven by a fundamental divergence between fast generative output and finite human state-space tracking. If developers surrender mental ownership for unverified speed, software teams risk accumulating opaque, unmaintainable systems that no human understands well enough to debug, secure, or evolve when AI abstractions fail.

articles.excerpt: Seven years later, a first watch of Tom Hooper’s Cats on Netflix finds plenty to enjoy, especially Taylor Swift’s catnip number.
articles.body: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
